groups.name: Booba Team
groups.profile: Ransomware.live lists it as "Booba Project" with the alias "Booba Team" (tracked since 2026-07-06). Today it posted a batch of US public-sector and non-profit victims, each with a stated stolen-data volume (under 1 GB to 295 GB).

groups.name: Qilin
groups.profile: Also known as Agenda. Golang/Rust RaaS active since July 2022 and one of the most prolific leak sites of 2025–26; double extortion, with the operator controlling encryption modes. Posted four victims on three continents in one batch, including a South Carolina city.
groups.countries: Japan, Spain, United Kingdom, not disclosed (1)

groups.name: Shiba
groups.profile: Leak site tracked since 2026-07-27, with no published tactics profile. Three of today's four postings appear only on Ransomware.live and carry no country.
groups.sectors: Agriculture & Food Production, Healthcare, Professional Services

groups.name: Emperador
groups.profile: Leak site tracked since 2026-08-12. Postings include scheduled publication dates, sample-file links and short negotiation deadlines, and say data was also encrypted.

groups.name: Rhysida
groups.profile: RaaS since May 2023; phishing and Cobalt Strike for access; sells stolen data in auction-style "lots".

groups.name: Scarlettgroup
groups.profile: Tracked only since 2026-10-08; uploads leaks to the QU.AX file host. Both of today's postings are bare domains with no data description.

groups.name: Dire Wolf
groups.profile: Human-operated Golang ransomware (Curve25519/ChaCha20) first documented in May 2025; tight core team rather than a broad affiliate programme; manufacturing and technology focus across 13+ countries, ransoms reported up to $500,000.

groups.name: Everstake
groups.profile: New on Ransomware.live today (added 2026-10-29). Posts carry category, size and a scheduled release date. Three of its four postings are masked domains (see Exclusions).

groups.name: Global Secret Group
groups.profile: Also known as GSG; tracked since 2026-07-26 with little public profile. Postings carry a templated country/revenue/size header.

groups.name: Interlock
groups.profile: Double-extortion group first seen September 2024; uses fake browser-update and ClickFix lures; heavy focus on healthcare, government and education across North America and Europe.

groups.name: Krybit
groups.profile: RaaS launched late March 2026 with an 80/20 affiliate split and Windows/Linux/ESXi/NAS lockers; known for a public feud with rival 0APT in which each leaked the other's operator data.

groups.name: Leakeddata
groups.profile: RansomLook's label for a leak site that mirrors SilentRansomGroup's postings on Ransomware.live (see №67).

groups.name: Whitearmor
groups.profile: New DLS tracked since 2026-10-20. Posts large consumer and corporate datasets in a mocking tone. This time it explicitly says it is not asking for a ransom.
